home.hook_kicker: Child sexual abuse in India — what the data says
home.hook_title: In {n} of every 100 cases, the child knew the person.
home.hook_sub: Not a stranger. A relative, a neighbour, a family friend, someone online, someone trusted.
home.scale_perday: That is about {perday} cases a day — one every {mins} minutes, on average across the year.
home.scale_dot_caption: Each dot is {per} registered cases. {dots} dots in all.
home.scale_tn: In Tamil Nadu, police registered {tn} POCSO cases in {year} — about {perday} a day.
home.scale_tn_note: Same NCRB table as the national figure. Tamil Nadu's own Police Policy Note reports the same total.
home.scale_rising: Rising numbers can mean more children and families are coming forward — not only more abuse. Tamil Nadu's rise is widely linked to stronger reporting.
home.who_title: Most offenders were people the child already knew.
home.who_lead: Of {total} cases under the most serious POCSO sections (4 & 6) in {year}, the offender was known to the child in {known} — {pct}%.
home.who_cat_family_friends_neighbours_known: Family friends, neighbours, employers and other known adults
home.who_cat_friends_online_partners: Friends, online friends, or partners “on the promise of marriage”
home.who_explainer_title: About the “friends, online friends and partners” group
home.who_explainer: POCSO treats all sexual activity with anyone under 18 as an offence, whether or not the child agreed. So this group mixes very different situations: grooming, online exploitation, and relationships between teenagers. The data cannot separate them. It is the largest group, but it should not be read as “22,000 predatory friends”.
home.who_explainer_2: For younger children, the groups that matter most are the clearest ones: family members, and family friends, neighbours and other known adults. Together they account for {n} cases in {year}. Teachers are counted inside “other known persons” — NCRB does not publish a separate school category.
home.who_tn_pending: Tamil Nadu breakdown: pending. NCRB publishes this table state by state; it will appear here once the {year} table is added to the data pipeline.
home.who_action: Teach your child that rules about their body apply to everyone — including people they love and trust. Nobody is an exception: not a relative, not a teacher, not a friend, not someone online.
home.age_title: Most registered victims are teenagers. The youngest are the least able to tell anyone.
home.age_lead: In {year}, {share}% of child victims in cases under POCSO's most serious sections (4 & 6) were aged 12–18.
home.age_note: Small numbers for young children do not mean young children are safe. A five-year-old may not have words for what happened, or may not know it was wrong. These bands are likely the most under-counted.
home.age_action: Start early and keep it ordinary. For little ones: correct names for body parts, and “no secrets from Amma and Appa”. For older children: consent, online safety, and that they can always tell you — even if they broke a rule.
home.justice_title: Justice is slow. The law's one-year limit is routinely missed.
home.justice_lead: The POCSO Act asks courts to finish a trial within one year, as far as possible. In practice, most cases wait much longer.
home.justice_tn_callout: {pending} POCSO cases were waiting for trial in Tamil Nadu. {over} of them — more than half — had waited longer than the one year the law allows.
home.justice_clock_actual: Average actual time to dispose a case
home.justice_clock_note: Average across about 4 lakh POCSO cases filed between 2012 and 2021 (research estimate, not a live figure).
home.justice_ftsc_title: Fast-track special courts are falling further behind
home.justice_ftsc_lead: In {year}, {registered} cases came into India's fast-track special courts and {disposed} were disposed. The pile of pending cases grew to {pending}.
home.justice_ftsc_note: Fast-track special courts hear rape and POCSO cases. {courts} were working as of {date}, including {pocso} that hear only POCSO cases.
home.justice_funnel_pending: Police-to-court funnel (chargesheets, convictions, acquittals) for {year}: pending. It appears here once the NCRB disposal tables are added to the pipeline. Conviction rate will always be shown next to pendency.
home.justice_action: A slow system means prevention and early disclosure matter even more. The best protection is a child who knows they will be believed — and a parent who knows what to do next.
home.act_title: What you can do this week
home.act_lead: Seven things that make children safer. None of them need you to be afraid — only to talk.
home.act_1_t: Teach the correct names for private body parts.
home.act_1_b: Children who have the words can tell you what happened. Use the real names, calmly, like any other part of the body.
home.act_2_t: Rules about their body apply to everyone.
home.act_2_b: Relatives, teachers, coaches, family friends, older children, people online. Loving someone does not give them an exception.
home.act_3_t: “We don't keep secrets in our family.”
home.act_3_b: Surprises are fine — they are fun and they end. Secrets that an adult asks a child to keep from parents are not.
home.act_4_t: Name three trusted adults your child can tell.
home.act_4_b: Ask your child to choose them with you. If one person doesn't listen, they tell the next.
home.act_5_t: If your child tells you something: stay calm and believe them.
home.act_5_b: Thank them for telling you. Don't blame them. Don't confront the person yourself. Report it — call 1098 or 112.
home.act_6_b: Sudden changes in behaviour or sleep, new fear of a particular person or place, or knowledge of sexual things that is unusual for their age. Signs are not proof — but they are a reason to listen closely.
home.act_7_t: Know who they talk to online.
home.act_7_b: Keep devices in shared spaces for younger children. For older ones, talk about people who ask for photos or secrecy — and make it clear they will not be punished for telling you.

help.childline_desc: 24×7, free. For any child who needs care and protection — or an adult worried about one.
help.erss_desc: Police, ambulance, fire. Use if a child is in danger right now.
help.cyber_desc: Report online sexual abuse or exploitation material involving children. You can report anonymously in the women/children section.
help.ncpcr_desc: Online complaint channel of the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights.
help.tncpcr_name: Tamil Nadu State Commission for Protection of Child Rights
help.tncpcr_desc: State child-rights commission. Contact details on their official page.
help.cwc_desc: Every district has one. Reach it through Childline 1098 or your district collectorate.
help.link_only: Links open official sites. We never embed complaint forms.
help.unverified_contact: We could not independently verify phone numbers for this office — use the official page.

explore.tn_trend_title: POCSO cases registered in Tamil Nadu, by year
explore.tn_trend_takeaway: Registered cases have more than doubled since 2020 — a rise that officials and child-rights groups widely link to more cases being reported.
explore.tn_trend_gap: No figure published in our sources for {year}.
explore.tn_ytd_body: Police told the press that {y2} saw {v2} POCSO cases in January–July, against {v1} in the same months of {y1}. These numbers are not yet in an official publication and are not used anywhere else on this site.
explore.tn_district_pending: District-wise figures appear here once the TN SCRB Crime Review or NCRB district tables are committed. The Madras High Court has also ordered a district-wise report on POCSO courts — it will become the district pendency layer when filed.
explore.tn_district_boundaries: Map uses Census 2011 district boundaries (32 districts). The six districts formed in 2019–2020 are drawn inside their parent district until an open 38-district boundary file is added.
explore.chennai_convictions: {n} people were convicted in {year} in POCSO cases registered by Greater Chennai Police.
explore.online_body: In {year}, the US-based NCMEC CyberTipline received {n} reports of suspected child sexual exploitation linked to India.
explore.online_caveat: Reports are not victims or cases. Most come from platforms' automated detection, and India's large online population drives volume.
explore.compare_soon: Side-by-side comparison of states and districts is planned once the state-wise series is in.
